chunks.chunk_text: The BRICS New Development Bank has approved over $5 billion in local-currency loans since 2023, signaling a decisive shift away from dollar-denominated lending among member states. The bank's president confirmed that 40% of its portfolio is now in non-USD instruments.

China and Russia have settled 65% of their bilateral trade in yuan and roubles as of Q1 2026, up from just 15% in 2020. The trend reflects coordinated central bank swap lines and a shared geopolitical interest in reducing US dollar exposure.

Google's Willow quantum processor achieved 105 qubits with error correction below the surface code threshold, marking the first demonstration of a logical qubit with error rates low enough for practical quantum computation at scale.

The EU AI Act has entered into force with tiered compliance requirements. High-risk AI systems must pass conformity assessments including bias audits and transparency reporting before deployment. Non-compliance fines reach 7% of global annual turnover.

ITER achieved first plasma in 2025 sustaining 150 million degrees Celsius for over six minutes. The milestone validates the tokamak design and clears the path toward deuterium-tritium fusion experiments scheduled for 2030.

Solid-state battery prototypes from QuantumScape achieved 500 Wh/kg energy density, doubling current lithium-ion performance. Samsung SDI and CATL have announced mass production timelines targeting 2027 for automotive-grade cells.

NASA's Artemis III mission successfully landed astronauts at the lunar south pole, collecting 85 kg of regolith samples from permanently shadowed regions. The mission confirmed water ice concentrations of 5.6% in Shackleton crater.

The US executive order on AI safety mandates that all foundation models trained with compute exceeding 10^26 FLOPs must undergo government-supervised red-teaming before public release. The order establishes a new AI Safety Institute for enforcement.

Commonwealth Fusion Systems completed construction of its SPARC tokamak using high-temperature superconducting magnets. The project aims to demonstrate net-positive energy from fusion by 2027 with a Q value exceeding 10.

India proposed a BRICS-wide digital currency platform designed to bypass the SWIFT messaging system. The initiative, backed by all member states at the 2025 summit, would enable real-time settlement in centrally issued digital currencies.

SpaceX Starship completed its first orbital refueling demonstration, transferring 50 metric tons of propellant between two docked Starships in low Earth orbit. The achievement is critical for NASA's Artemis program and deep space missions.

China's Chang'e-7 mission returned 2.1 kg of samples from the lunar far side, including the first-ever samples from the South Pole-Aitken basin. Preliminary analysis reveals unique mineral compositions not found in near-side samples.

The BRICS share of global foreign exchange reserves has risen to 35% according to the latest IMF data, compared to 28% in 2020. The shift reflects coordinated reserve diversification by central banks in emerging economies.

TAE Technologies announced a breakthrough in hydrogen-boron fusion, achieving a stable plasma at 200 million degrees for 30 seconds. The aneutronic approach promises reduced radioactive waste compared to deuterium-tritium reactions.
Saudi Arabia and the UAE have formally joined the BRICS settlement mechanism, agreeing to denominate 30% of their bilateral oil trade in currencies other than the US dollar beginning January 2026.

MIT researchers demonstrated a high-temperature superconducting magnet capable of 20 tesla, a record for fusion-grade magnets. The technology reduces the size and cost of future tokamak reactors by an estimated 40%.

Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket reached orbit on its maiden launch, delivering a prototype communications satellite to geostationary transfer orbit. The reusable first stage successfully landed on the drone ship 'Jacklyn'.

The UK Atomic Energy Authority selected the STEP fusion prototype site at West Burton, with construction expected to begin in 2027. The spherical tokamak design aims for a Q value of 4 with a compact footprint.

Brazil is leading efforts to establish a BRICS common unit of account for intra-bloc trade settlements, separate from any national currency. The proposal has drawn interest from 12 additional nations seeking observer status.

Zap Energy reached 37 million degrees in its sheared-flow-stabilized Z-pinch reactor. While below fusion temperatures, the company claims it demonstrates confinement stability sufficient for a commercial breakeven reactor.

CATL unveiled a sodium-ion battery with 200 Wh/kg energy density targeted at entry-level EVs. The technology uses abundant raw materials and offers better cold-weather performance than lithium-iron-phosphate batteries.

Japan published AI guidelines focusing on economic competitiveness rather than strict regulation. The framework encourages private-sector self-regulation with government oversight for critical infrastructure applications.

Helion Energy signed a power purchase agreement with Microsoft for fusion-generated electricity by 2028, claiming its sixth-generation plasma accelerator can achieve breakeven at one-tenth the cost of tokamak designs.

General Fusion demonstrated its plasma injector technology at the UK STEP prototype site, achieving the required density and temperature targets for the magnetized target fusion approach in repeated 3-millisecond pulses.

The JWST discovered carbon compounds, including methane and carbon dioxide, on Europa's surface using its NIRSpec instrument. The finding strengthens the case for a habitable subsurface ocean and supports the Europa Clipper mission.

BYD's blade battery passed extreme safety tests including nail penetration and overcharge, demonstrating no thermal runaway. The LFP-based battery has become standard in BYD's entire passenger EV lineup since 2024.
South Africa reported that BRICS membership has boosted its trade with Asian member states by 25% since joining, particularly in commodities including platinum group metals and agricultural products.

The US AI Safety Institute published its first testing standards for frontier models, requiring red-teaming results, capability assessments, and safety evaluations before model weights can be distributed publicly.
Tesla's 4680 battery cells reached full production at Giga Texas with yields exceeding 95%, enabling the Cybertruck and long-range versions of the Model Y to achieve EPA ranges above 400 miles.

The NIF achieved net energy gain in a second fusion ignition experiment, producing 3.5 MJ from 2.1 MJ of laser input. The result confirms reproducibility of the December 2022 breakthrough using updated target designs.

UK AI regulation relies on existing sector regulators rather than creating a new AI-specific body. The approach emphasises principles-based guidance over statutory rules, drawing criticism from civil society groups.

Private fusion investment exceeded $6 billion globally in 2025 according to the Fusion Industry Association, with Commonwealth Fusion Systems, Helion, and TAE Technologies accounting for 60% of total funding.

QuantumScape shipped its first solid-state battery samples to automotive partners for qualification testing. The samples use a ceramic separator with lithium-metal anode technology that the company claims enables fast charging.
The IMF reported that central bank gold purchases reached 1,000 metric tons in 2025, driven by emerging market central banks diversifying away from US Treasury holdings amid geopolitical uncertainty.

China's AI regulations emphasize content control and algorithmic transparency, requiring all generative AI services to register training data sources and implement real-time content filtering for sensitive topics.

A new report claims that the European Central Bank has developed a prototype digital euro capable of processing 100,000 transactions per second, positioning it as a potential competitor to private payment systems.

The US Department of Energy allocated $500 million for fusion energy research in fiscal year 2026, with funding directed toward public-private partnerships for milestone-based reactor development programs.

Industry analysts project that solid-state battery production costs will decline to $75/kWh by 2030 as manufacturing scale increases, down from an estimated $400/kWh in 2025 according to BloombergNEF.

China launched a new remote sensing satellite constellation for environmental monitoring, claiming the 50-satellite network can detect methane leaks and track deforestation with daily global coverage.
South Korea announced a $700 million investment in quantum computing research over the next five years, targeting the development of a 1,000-qubit fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2030.
The European Commission proposed a new classification system for AI training data that would require companies to disclose whether datasets include copyrighted material or personal information.

A study published in Nature Materials describes a new electrolyte composition for lithium-sulfur batteries that maintains 85% capacity after 500 charge cycles, addressing the historical rapid degradation problem.
EV sales in Europe grew 18% year-over-year in Q1 2026, with market share reaching 28% of new vehicle registrations. Germany and France accounted for the majority of sales growth across the region.
A team at Stanford demonstrated a new machine learning algorithm that can predict protein folding with 95% accuracy, reducing computation time from days to hours compared to AlphaFold2.

The World Economic Forum published a report identifying AI-enabled cyberattacks as the top global risk for 2026, citing generative AI's potential to automate sophisticated phishing and social engineering campaigns.

India's Chandrayaan-4 mission successfully deployed a rover at the lunar south pole, transmitting high-resolution images of shadowed craters and confirming the presence of water ice in surface regolith.

Global semiconductor sales reached $600 billion in 2025, driven by AI accelerator demand and automotive chip content growth. TSMC and Samsung both reported record revenue from advanced node manufacturing.
The WHO issued new guidelines for AI in healthcare, requiring clinical validation studies for diagnostic algorithms and mandating human oversight for all treatment recommendation systems.

A carbon capture facility in Iceland became operational, capable of removing 4,000 tons of CO2 per year using direct air capture technology powered entirely by geothermal energy from the Hellisheidi plant.
Archaeologists in Egypt discovered a 4,000-year-old funerary complex near Luxor containing well-preserved wall paintings and burial chambers, shedding new light on Middle Kingdom funerary practices.
